title: Optometry work experience
subtitle: Birmingham & Solihull — beyond the high street. Hospitals, surgical and community eye care, specialist independents, and sight loss charities.
checkedNote: Contact details checked 18 October 2026 from each organisation's own site or official listings. Confirm before sending.
howTo: Lead with being an Aston optometry student — say your year, when you're free, and what you'd like to observe (e.g. glaucoma clinic, contact lens fits, low vision).
Where there's no public email, call and ask for the practice manager or clinical lead, then follow up by email.
For NHS trusts, contact both the work experience/volunteering team and the eye department. Expect paperwork (DBS, occupational health, confidentiality).
Ask your Aston placement team too — several places here already have links with the university.

startWith.why: Already runs a low vision partnership with Aston, so it's an open door.
The big hospital option, with its own optometry department.
Run by an optometrist who became an Advanced Clinical Practitioner in ophthalmology, so it shows where an optometry career can go. (Not to be confused with Edgbaston Eye Consultants.)

beforeYouSend: Some places have no public email. Private surgical clinics like SpaMedica, Optegra and Midland Eye only have contact forms — call and ask for the practice manager. Dickens Eye Clinic is the opposite: an email but no phone number.

Double-check a few phone numbers. The Optical Express and ACES numbers come from their CQC (health regulator) registrations, the Perspective Opticians number from an online directory, and the Solihull Talking Newspaper details from the Charity Commission register — not their own websites.
University Hospitals Birmingham: the work experience email came from one of its older pages, so use the online request form as well.
BMEC's trust scheme is currently closed. That's why a direct, polite approach to the optometry department is the best route for now.

categories.title: Hospital eye departments
categories.intro: Biggest learning value. NHS trusts usually route student requests through a work experience or volunteering team, so contact both that team and the department.

places.name: Birmingham and Midland Eye Centre (BMEC)
places.address: City Health Campus (formerly City Hospital), Dudley Road, Birmingham B18 7QH
places.description: One of the largest eye centres in Europe. Eye A&E plus cataract, cornea, glaucoma, oculoplastics, paediatrics, vitreo-retinal and visual electrophysiology. Its own optometry department does complex and paediatric refraction, medical contact lenses, low vision aids and glaucoma / medical retina shared care.

phones.note: Mon–Fri, 9am–4pm — ask for the Optometry Department (open 8.30am–4.30pm)

places.tip: The trust's formal work experience scheme opens in rounds online and is currently closed — so a direct, polite approach to the optometry team is worth trying in the meantime.

places.name: University Hospitals Birmingham — Ophthalmology
places.address: Heartlands Hospital (Bordesley Green East, B9 5ST), Solihull Hospital (Lode Lane, B91 2JL) and Good Hope Hospital eye clinic
places.description: Around 80 staff including ophthalmologists, optometrists, orthoptists, ophthalmic nurses, medical photographers and technicians. Sub-specialties include cornea, glaucoma, cataract, medical retina / diabetes, macular degeneration, squints, oculoplastics and artificial eyes.
places.tip: UHB says it closes applications when oversubscribed, so apply early. The email above is from an older UHB page — use the online form too.

places.name: Queen Elizabeth Hospital Birmingham (QEHB) — Ophthalmology
places.address: Mindelsohn Way, Edgbaston, Birmingham B15 2WB
places.description: Major teaching hospital with its own ophthalmology department in Outpatients Area 1: 14 consultant ophthalmologists, outpatient clinics and day-case surgery, supported by orthoptics, optometry, a Low Vision Refraction Service and a Low Vision Nurse Service.

phones.note: Switchboard — ask for Ophthalmology / Outpatients Area 1

emails.label: UHB work experience team — same trust as above

places.tip: QEHB is a short trip from Aston and the low vision refraction service is a great fit for an optometry student.

places.name: Birmingham Children's Hospital — Eye Department
places.address: Steelhouse Lane, Birmingham B4 6NH
places.description: Specialist paediatric eye unit with nationally commissioned retinoblastoma and paediatric ocular oncology services. Team of 4 consultant ophthalmologists, 12 orthoptists, 2 nurses and 3 optometrists; also runs retinopathy of prematurity screening at the Women's Hospital.
places.tip: BWC doesn't run placements in school holidays or weekends, and caps them at two weeks.

categories.title: Surgical and community eye care
categories.intro: Cataract, laser and community ophthalmology providers employ optometrists for pre- and post-op checks, so they're great for seeing the clinical side outside a hospital.

places.name: SpaMedica — Birmingham & Solihull
places.address: Apex House, 3 Embassy Drive, Calthorpe Rd, Edgbaston B15 1TR | Cornwall House, Blythe Valley Park, Solihull B90 8AF
places.description: The UK's largest provider of NHS cataract surgery. Both sites also treat wet AMD, diabetic macular oedema and retinal vein occlusion, and do YAG laser. Runs an accredited partner programme and CPD for community optometrists.
places.emailNote: No public email found — use the website contact form or call (the form has a 'Job/careers enquiry' option).

places.name: Optegra Eye Hospital Birmingham
places.address: Aston University Campus, Coleshill Street, Birmingham B4 7ET
places.description: Dedicated eye hospital doing laser eye surgery, lens replacement and cataract surgery for NHS and private patients. It sits on Aston's own campus and has sponsored Aston optometry and ophthalmology workshops.
places.emailNote: No public email found — use the website contact form or call.
places.tip: Being on her campus is a natural opener — mention you're an Aston optometry student.

places.name: Newmedica Birmingham
places.address: Aqueous One, Aston Cross Business Village, Rocky Lane, Birmingham B6 5RQ
places.description: Consultant-led eye clinic and surgical centre doing NHS and private cataract surgery, glaucoma, AMD, epiretinal membrane / vitreoretinal surgery, oculoplastics and YAG laser. Open Mon–Fri 8am–6pm.

places.name: CHEC (Community Health and Eyecare) — Kings Norton
places.address: Kingsgate House, Pershore Road, Kings Norton, Birmingham B30 3EP
places.description: One of the larger community ophthalmology providers in the UK, delivering NHS cataract surgery and ophthalmology outside hospital. Also has a West Bromwich site just outside Birmingham.
places.emailNote: No public email found — use the website contact form or call.

places.name: Midland Eye
places.address: 50 Lode Lane, Solihull B91 2AW
places.description: Private eye surgery centre set up by teaching-hospital consultant surgeons. Laser eye surgery, cataract, lens exchange, ICL, glaucoma, keratoconus, retinal and oculoplastic treatment. CQC rated Good, with Well-led rated Outstanding.
places.emailNote: No public email found — use the website contact form or call.

places.name: Optical Express — Birmingham Hospital
places.address: 16 Corporation Street, Birmingham B2 4RN
places.description: Laser and refractive surgery clinic rated Outstanding overall by the CQC. A good place to see refractive assessments and post-op care.

phones.note: As listed with the CQC — double-check

places.emailNote: No public email found — use the website contact form or call.

places.name: Edgbaston Eye Consultants
places.address: The George Road Clinic, 22 George Road, Edgbaston B15 1PJ
places.description: Consultant-led private ophthalmology clinic: cataract, glaucoma, oculoplastics, intravitreal injections, retina, neuro-ophthalmology, refractive surgery, ICL and dry eye. CQC rated Good, with Effective rated Outstanding.

places.name: The Westbourne Centre (Ramsay Health Care)
places.address: 53 Church Road, Edgbaston, Birmingham B15 3SJ
places.description: Private day-surgery and outpatient centre where consultant ophthalmologists see NHS and private patients for cataracts, lens replacement, corneal problems, YAG laser and laser eye surgery.
places.emailNote: No public email found — use the website contact form or call (staff emails exist but are personal — call admin first).

places.name: Spire Little Aston Hospital — Eye Surgery
places.address: Little Aston Hall Drive, Sutton Coldfield B74 3UP (just over the Birmingham boundary, near Mere Green)
places.description: Private hospital with a large ophthalmology team: cataract and multifocal lens surgery, cornea and keratoconus cross-linking, complex and minimally invasive glaucoma surgery, refractive and laser surgery, eyelid and orbital surgery, thyroid eye disease, retina and intravitreal injections.
places.emailNote: No public email found — use the website contact form or call.
places.tip: Technically in Staffordshire, but it has a Sutton Coldfield address and is easy to reach from north Birmingham.

places.name: Optimax — Birmingham City Centre
places.address: Edmund House, 12–22 Newhall Street, Birmingham B3 3AS
places.description: Laser and lens surgery provider. The city-centre clinic handles consultations and aftercare, which is where optometrists do refractive assessments and post-op checks.

places.name: Midland Health — Dry Eye Laser Clinic
places.address: 78–79 Francis Road, Edgbaston B16 8SP and Harborne Hospital, Mindelsohn Way B15 2FQ
places.description: Private clinic running a dry eye service with Edgbaston Eye Consultants: IPL laser for meibomian gland dysfunction, LipiFlow thermal pulsation, and consultant ophthalmology consultations, plus paediatric ophthalmology.

places.name: Spire Parkway Hospital — Eye Surgery
places.address: 1 Damson Parkway, Solihull B91 2PP
places.description: Private hospital with a busy ophthalmology team offering rapid-access eye care. Treats cataract, glaucoma (including trabeculectomy), AMD, retinal detachment and macular holes, squint, keratoconus (corneal cross-linking), dry eye, eyelid problems, laser eye surgery and refractive lens exchange.
places.emailNote: No public email found — use the website contact form or call.
places.tip: Ask for the outpatients or ophthalmology manager — private hospitals often host students via a consultant who agrees to be shadowed.

places.name: The Priory Hospital (Circle Health Group)
places.address: Priory Road, Edgbaston, Birmingham B5 7UG
places.description: The largest private hospital in Birmingham. Its outpatient department hosts consultant ophthalmologists, with imaging on site for fast diagnosis.
places.emailNote: No public email found — use the website contact form or call.

places.name: ACES Birmingham (Anglia Community Eye Service)
places.address: 16 Corporation Street, Birmingham B2 4RN
places.description: Community eye service delivering NHS ophthalmology outside hospital — diagnostic tests, treatment and minor surgical procedures for adults referred by optometrists and GPs.

phones.note: As listed with the CQC — double-check

places.emailNote: No public email found — use the website contact form or call.

places.name: Birmingham Community Healthcare — Paediatric Eye Service
places.address: Clinics at Broadmeadow (Kings Norton), Northfield, Quinton Lane and Hall Green health centres
places.description: NHS community team of orthoptists and paediatric optometrists assessing and treating children's vision and eye co-ordination problems across South Birmingham. Runs eye care in six special schools, a Down syndrome clinic, and clinics at child development centres.
places.emailNote: No public email found — use the website contact form or call.
places.tip: Brilliant for paediatric and special-needs experience you won't get on the high street.

categories.title: Specialist independent practices
categories.intro: Independents focused on contact lenses, myopia management or dry eye — more likely to take a student than chains, and more interesting cases.

places.name: Edgbaston Eye Clinic
places.address: The Consulting Rooms, 38 Harborne Road, Edgbaston B15 3HE
places.description: Founded in 2017 by Don Williams, an optometrist who became an Advanced Clinical Practitioner in ophthalmology and previously worked at BMEC. Glaucoma, dry eye, keratoconus, medical retina, eye moles, YAG and SLT laser, plus specialist contact lenses (RGP, scleral, ortho-K referrals).
places.tip: A brilliant example of how far an optometry career can go — worth saying that in her email.

places.name: James Ernest Optometry
places.address: 26 The Circle, Harborne, Birmingham B17 9DY
places.description: Specialist practice run by Bradley Warwick, an Aston graduate and specialist independent prescribing optometrist. Myopia management, ortho-K, scleral lenses, binocular vision, glaucoma, and community ophthalmology with a UHB consultant.

places.name: EYE Opticians — Edgbaston
places.address: 44 Islington Row, Edgbaston, Birmingham B15 1LD
places.description: Family-run independent with 40 years in Birmingham. Dry eye clinic with OptiLight IPL, visual stress / colorimetry, myopia control, a contact lens centre for complex fits, and OCT and visual field testing.

places.name: Dickens Eye Clinic
places.address: 39 Main Street, Dickens Heath, Solihull B90 1UB
places.description: Boutique independent in Solihull doing ortho-K, myopia control, specialist contact lens fitting, OCT scanning and eye health monitoring. Open Tue–Sat, 9am–5pm.
places.phoneNote: Not listed on their website — email first.

places.name: Pabari Opticians
places.address: 14 St Mary's Row, Moseley, Birmingham B13 8JG
places.description: Family-run practice for over 40 years. Myopia management, specialised contact lens fitting with corneal topography, OCT and Optomap imaging, colorimetry and children's eye exams.
places.emailNote: No public email found — use the website contact form or call.

places.name: Aston University Eye Clinic
places.address: Vision Sciences, Aston University, Aston Triangle, Birmingham B4 7ET
places.description: Her own uni's clinic — around 8,000 patient episodes a year, open to the public, with low vision assessments and specialist clinics. Worth asking about extra shadowing, research assistant or clinic support roles.
places.emailNote: Ask via your course team or the clinic directly.

places.name: The Contact Lens Practice
places.address: 5 Lower Temple Street (1st floor), Birmingham B2 4JD
places.description: City-centre specialist contact lens practice that takes referrals from the eye hospital. Keratoconus (RGP, hybrid, piggyback, scleral and semi-scleral lenses, plus cross-linking referrals), ortho-K, myopia control, bespoke lenses for complex prescriptions and corneal dystrophy.
places.emailNote: No public email found — use the website contact form or call.
places.tip: Ideal if she's keen on contact lenses — specialty fitting like this is hard to see anywhere else.

places.name: Perspective Opticians
places.address: High Street, Knowle, Solihull B93 0LF
places.description: Award-winning independent in Solihull since 2005. Advanced eye examinations with OCT 3D scans, myopia control, children's eye care and advanced contact lens fitting.

phones.note: From an online directory listing — check on their website

places.emailNote: No public email found — use the website contact form or call.

places.name: Kings Opticians
places.address: 1–3 Pershore Road South, Cotteridge, Birmingham B30 3EE
places.description: Independent practice with a dry eye clinic, myopia control, OCT eye scans, children's eye tests, contact lenses, and the NHS CUES urgent eye care service.

places.name: The Eye Collective — Harborne
places.address: 154 High Street, Harborne, Birmingham B17 9PN
places.description: Sister practice to The Contact Lens Practice. Myopia management plans for children, dry eye assessments, contact lens aftercare, comprehensive and children's eye exams, and bespoke digitally measured lenses.
places.emailNote: No public email found — use the website contact form or call.

places.name: Andrew Martin & Associates
places.address: 66 Boldmere Road, Sutton Coldfield B73 5TJ (plus a second practice on Lichfield Road)
places.description: Long-established independent (dating back to the 1960s) offering the NHS Minor Eye Conditions Service — red or sore eyes, flashes and floaters, sudden vision loss, foreign bodies — alongside digital eye photography and contact lenses.
places.tip: Minor eye conditions work is real clinical decision-making — great to observe.

places.name: Neil Berry Opticians
places.address: 6 Holland Street, Sutton Coldfield B72 1RR
places.description: Independent with 30+ years' experience and a City & Guilds approved centre for digital diabetic eye screening. Also does glaucoma checks, retinal photography and OCT imaging.
places.emailNote: No public email found — use the website contact form or call.

places.name: Lad & Turner Opticians
places.address: The Lanes Shopping Centre, Wylde Green, Sutton Coldfield B72 1YG
places.description: Independent offering urgent eye care, dry eye support, home eye tests for people who can't get to the practice, contact lenses, and hearing care.

places.name: Walford & Round Opticians
places.address: Dovehouse Parade, 363 Warwick Road, Solihull B91 1BQ
places.description: Family-owned Solihull practice listed in SeeAbility's directory of optometrists who welcome people with learning disabilities, with wheelchair access to the testing room.
places.tip: Good for learning how to adapt eye exams for patients with learning disabilities or autism.

categories.title: Low vision and sight loss charities
categories.intro: Volunteering here builds communication skills and low vision understanding, and many roles are flexible around uni.

places.name: Focus Birmingham
places.address: 48–62 Woodville Road, Harborne, Birmingham B17 9AT
places.description: Birmingham's main sight loss charity, going since 1846. Runs a Low Vision Centre and clinic, counselling, befriending, rehabilitation, and an aids and technology shop. It already partners with Aston to train optometry students in a real low vision setting, and advertises volunteer roles like telephone befriender.
places.tip: Probably the strongest fit on this list — ask specifically about the low vision clinic.

places.name: Queen Alexandra College (QAC)
places.address: Court Oak Road, Harborne, Birmingham B17 9TG
places.description: National specialist college for 16–25 year olds, originally founded to educate blind and visually impaired young people. Has a Visual Impairment Training Officer and rehabilitation and travel trainers on site, and runs the Sight Village assistive technology exhibitions.

places.name: BID Services
places.address: Deaf Cultural Centre, Ladywood Road, Birmingham B16 8SZ
places.description: Sensory impairment charity that runs Birmingham Sensory Services (with Focus Birmingham) and Solihull Sensory Services, including sight loss rehabilitation and mobility training.

places.name: Guide Dogs — Birmingham team
places.address: Midlands region
places.description: As well as guide dogs, runs 'My Guide', matching volunteer sighted guides with visually impaired people. Volunteers must be 18+ and have an enhanced DBS check.

places.name: RNIB Eye Care Support Service (Eye Clinic Liaison Officers)
places.address: Based in Birmingham's eye clinics — BMEC, QEHB, Heartlands, Solihull and Good Hope
places.description: RNIB's Eye Clinic Liaison Officers sit inside hospital eye clinics and support newly diagnosed patients with information, emotional support, registration and benefits advice. Shadowing one shows the human side of sight loss diagnoses.
places.tip: These are patient support lines — keep the message short and ask if a student could shadow for a day.

places.name: Birmingham Talking Newspapers
places.address: PO Box 15733, Sutton Coldfield B73 9TB
places.description: Free audio news service for blind and partially sighted people in and around Birmingham. Volunteers read local newspaper content, sent out online or on USB sticks.

places.name: Solihull Borough Talking Newspaper Association
places.address: Dorridge, Solihull
places.description: Small volunteer-run charity producing a weekly recorded newspaper for blind and partially sighted people across the Solihull borough.

phones.note: As listed on the Charity Commission register
